source_text: Sed qui dixerat: Petite et accipietis, petentibus dederat eum exitum quem quisque desiderauerat. Nam, si quando inter se de martyrii sui uoto sermocinabantur, Saturninus quidem omnibus bestiis uelle se obici profitebatur, ut scilicet gloriosiorem gestaret coronam. Itaque in commissione spectaculi ipse et Reuocatus leopardum experti etiam super pulpitum ab urso uexati sunt. Saturus autem nihil magis quam ursum abominabatur; sed uno morsu leopardi confici se iam praesumebat. Itaque cum apro subministraretur, uenator potius qui illum ad aprum subligauerat, subfossus ab eadem bestia post dies muneris obiit; Saturus solummodo tractus est. Et cum ad ursum substrictus esset in ponte, ursus de cauea prodire noluit. Itaque secundo Saturus inlaesus reuocatur.
thought_title: Each man gets the death he asked for
orientation: The redactor narrates how the men meet the wild beasts in the public games.
pass_a_gloss: But he who had said Ask and you will receive had given to them as they asked that end which each one had desired. For if at any time among themselves about the vow of their martyrdom they were talking, Saturninus indeed was professing that he wished himself to be thrown to all the wild beasts, so that clearly he might wear a more glorious crown. Therefore at the beginning of the show he himself and Revocatus experienced a leopard and also on the platform by a bear were mauled. But Saturus nothing more than a bear was hating; but by one bite of a leopard himself to be finished he was already expecting in advance. Therefore when he was being handed over to a boar, the hunter rather who had bound him to the boar, dug from below by the same wild beast after the days of the public games died; Saturus only was dragged. And when he had been tied up for a bear on the bridge, the bear from the cage refused to come out. Therefore for a second time Saturus unharmed is called back.

pass_b_english: But the one who had said, "Ask and you will receive" (John 16:24), had granted to them as they asked the outcome that each one had desired. For whenever they were talking together about the vow of their martyrdom, Saturninus for his part would openly declare that he wanted to be thrown to all the wild beasts, so that, of course, he would wear a more glorious crown. So at the opening of the show Saturninus himself and Revocatus faced a leopard and were also mauled by a bear on the platform. Saturus, however, loathed nothing more than the bear, but he was already expecting to be finished off by a single bite from a leopard. So when he was handed over to a boar, it was rather the hunter who had tied him to the boar who was gored from below by the same wild beast and died after the days of the public games; Saturus was only dragged. And when he had been bound fast for the bear on the bridge, the bear refused to come out of its cage. So for a second time Saturus is called back unharmed.
